specification.problem: Implement the oracle of Grover's quantum search over a real unstructured classical database as a simple circuit, where the oracle contains a quantumly accessible classical memory storing the database.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction only: oracle structure (classical memory queried in superposition) within Grover search; the specific gate-level circuit and memory design are not given in the abstract. Any finite instance is an assumed illustration.

symbols.meaning: Marking function; 1 if entry x satisfies the search criterion
Classical database content stored at address x

symbols.domain: unitary on index register plus ancilla

equations.label: Oracle phase action
equations.description: Standard Grover oracle flips the phase of marked items.
equations.justification: Standard Grover search definition; the abstract only mentions an oracle for Grover search.

equations.label: Memory query
equations.description: Quantumly accessible classical memory loads the data at address x in superposition.
equations.justification: Assumed model of the abstract's quantumly accessible classical memory; the exact construction is not stated.
assumptions: Memory acts as a controlled-load of D_x into a data register

equations.label: Oracle from memory
equations.description: The marking bit is computed from the stored data via a predicate g, then memory is uncomputed.
equations.justification: Assumed compute-phase-uncompute composition consistent with an oracle containing memory.
assumptions: Predicate g is a fixed classical function

registers.name: index
registers.role: Address register holding superposition over database indices

registers.name: data
registers.role: Receives D_x from the classical memory

registers.name: flag
registers.role: Ancilla in |-> for phase kickback of g(D_x)

specification.initial_state: Index register in uniform superposition via Hadamards, data in |0>, flag in |->.

steps.description: Apply memory query U_M to load D_x into the data register, entangled with the index.
Compute predicate g(D_x) onto the flag in |-> so phase (-1)^{f(x)} is kicked back.

Apply inverse memory query to uncompute the data register, leaving the net oracle action. Follow with the diffusion operator and repeat about (pi/4)sqrt(N/M) times for M marked items (sqrt(N) scale for M=1).

specification.measurement: Measure the index register in the computational basis after the Grover iterations.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Read the outcome as candidate index x, classically check g(D_x) against the database, and repeat the run if it is not marked.
assumptions: Oracle is built as memory query, marking, and uncompute.
Register sizes n, m, 1 and the single-flag layout are assumed, not from the abstract.
Standard Grover iteration count is used.
Equations are background or assumed; none are quoted from the abstract.
